contentKinds.essential: Broadly useful craft that belongs in the general PlotPickle journey.
contentKinds.deep-dive: Focused expansion of an existing craft area for learners who want more depth.
contentKinds.medium-extension: Craft whose rules are specific to a medium and must not be presented as universal screenplay law.
contentKinds.case-study: Rights-safe PlotPickle-authored analysis attached to a lesson; not imported screenplay or external case-study prose.
contentKinds.exercise: Applied activity attached to a lesson; not a separate canonical lesson.

authoringWaves.title: General craft bridges
authoringWaves.boundary: General-purpose gaps first; no television medium layer required.

authoringWaves.title: Television medium extensions
authoringWaves.boundary: Medium-specific teaching must be labeled as television/comedy craft rather than universal screenplay rules.

authoringWaves.title: Optional specialist enrichment
authoringWaves.boundary: Deferred. International traditions, comparative corpora and stage/opera material require a later explicit decision before any lesson ID is reserved or body is authored.

lessonCandidates.title: Scene Craft: Objective, Pressure and Turn
lessonCandidates.rationale: PlotPickle already teaches scene execution across drafting, dialogue, visual storytelling and revision; this lesson unifies those concepts into one deterministic scene-level diagnostic without replacing the existing lessons.
lessonCandidates.learningBoundary: Teach scene objective, pressure, turn, entry/exit choice, visual carrier and transition as connected craft decisions; do not impose a mandatory scene formula.

companionItems.title: Map objective, pressure and turn
companionItems.purpose: Apply the diagnostic to one scene from the learner's own story.

lessonCandidates.provenanceRequirement: Independently authored from PlotPickle's existing scene-related curriculum plus verified craft research; no external skill or screenplay prose copied.

lessonCandidates.title: Screenplay Format and Delivery
lessonCandidates.rationale: PlotPickle teaches screenplay language and drafting but lacks one concise lesson that connects readable spec-page conventions, document handoff and delivery readiness.
lessonCandidates.learningBoundary: Teach durable formatting principles and delivery questions; do not freeze software-specific commands, mutable contest rules or one jurisdiction's submission requirements into canon.

companionItems.title: Screenplay delivery audit
companionItems.purpose: Inspect a current draft for readability, consistency and delivery readiness.

lessonCandidates.provenanceRequirement: Use primary/authorized format guidance where practical and verify mutable delivery requirements at authoring/use time.

lessonCandidates.title: Adaptation: Source to Screen
lessonCandidates.rationale: Existing curriculum covers treatment, screenplay progression, provenance and ownership, but not the creative craft of transforming source material into screen action.
lessonCandidates.learningBoundary: Separate creative adaptation choices from legal rights advice. Teach selection, compression, expansion, point of view and cinematic transformation without implying that access to source material grants adaptation rights.

companionItems.title: Keep, compress, transform or omit
companionItems.purpose: Use a rights-safe invented source scenario to compare adaptation choices.

companionItems.title: Transform one source beat for screen
companionItems.purpose: Convert one prose/internal beat into visible and audible dramatic action.

lessonCandidates.provenanceRequirement: Use independently authored examples or public-domain/authorized material; retain rights/provenance boundaries explicitly.

lessonCandidates.title: Series Craft: Episode and Season Architecture
lessonCandidates.rationale: PlotPickle teaches structural diversity and episodic form generally but lacks a coherent television layer for episode, pilot and season movement.
lessonCandidates.learningBoundary: Teach teaser/cold-open choices, act-out logic, A/B/C story weaving, pilot architecture, season movement and streaming/broadcast differences as medium-specific options, not universal timing formulas.

companionItems.title: Broadcast, streaming and serialized form comparison
companionItems.purpose: Compare invented/right-safe episode structures without reproducing proprietary scripts.

companionItems.title: Weave A/B/C story movement
companionItems.purpose: Map three story lines across an episode and test convergence, contrast and pacing.

lessonCandidates.provenanceRequirement: Verify medium conventions from suitable primary/authorized sources and use rights-safe examples.

lessonCandidates.title: Series Engine and Bible Design
lessonCandidates.rationale: PlotPickle has story-bible, world and character-system concepts but no television-specific discipline for repeatable episode generation and series documents.
lessonCandidates.learningBoundary: Teach the series engine as a repeatable source of dramatic pressure, distinguish creative bible content from pitch/selling documents, and avoid treating one broadcaster/streamer document format as universal.

companionItems.title: Five-episode engine test
companionItems.purpose: Generate five distinct episode premises to test whether the engine produces repeatable conflict without repetition.

lessonCandidates.provenanceRequirement: External series/corpus material may inform research but must not be reproduced; examples should be PlotPickle-authored or rights-safe.

lessonCandidates.title: Writers' Room: Story Breaking and Notes
lessonCandidates.rationale: PlotPickle's collaboration curriculum is strong for ownership, handoff and review but does not teach the distinct creative workflow of a television writers' room.
lessonCandidates.learningBoundary: Teach story breaking, notes flow, role/authority boundaries, episode document handoffs and production constraints while preserving PlotPickle's Human approval and contribution boundaries.

companionItems.title: Break an episode as a room
companionItems.purpose: Simulate a bounded story-break workflow with explicit roles, proposals and Human approval.

lessonCandidates.provenanceRequirement: Verify current role/industry claims from suitable first-party or authorized sources where practical; do not encode mutable employment terms as timeless rules.

lessonCandidates.title: Half-Hour Comedy Craft
lessonCandidates.rationale: General PlotPickle structure and dialogue tools apply to comedy, but sitcom/half-hour craft has distinct structural and comic mechanisms that deserve an explicitly medium-specific extension.
lessonCandidates.learningBoundary: Teach premise-driven comic pressure, setup/payoff, escalation, running devices and single-/multi-camera considerations without reducing comedy to a mandatory joke count or format grid.

companionItems.title: Escalating a comic beat
companionItems.purpose: Use an invented scene to compare successive comic revisions without copying published material.

companionItems.title: Setup and payoff pass
companionItems.purpose: Track setup, expectation, turn and payoff through one learner-owned comic scene.

lessonCandidates.provenanceRequirement: Use PlotPickle-authored examples and treat mutable production-format conventions as externally verifiable context.

lessonCandidates.title: Professional Practice: Pitching and Representation
lessonCandidates.rationale: The current Industry curriculum establishes organizations, rights and verification habits but remains thin on pitching, querying, representation and career-facing decision making.
lessonCandidates.learningBoundary: Teach purpose, preparation, communication and verification habits for pitches, queries, representation, options/credits concepts and career resilience; do not provide legal advice or freeze current rates/rules into curriculum.

companionItems.title: Pitch and query readiness check
companionItems.purpose: Prepare a truthful project-specific communication package and identify claims that require current external verification.

lessonCandidates.provenanceRequirement: Current guild, representation, credit, option and contract claims must be verified against official/current sources at authoring and use time.

deferredEnrichment.reason: Valuable comparative craft, but it should follow the core and television gaps and needs careful source/provenance design to avoid flattening distinct traditions.
Use only independently authored analysis with public-domain, licensed, authorized or invented examples; no external case-study/script corpus import.
Specialist medium craft should remain optional and should not displace PlotPickle's screenwriting core.
